claims.text: The presence or absence of ferromagnetic ground states can be determined using ab initio molecular dynamics simulations.
The proposed calculations use the generalized gradient approximation with the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functional.
Electronic structure is the mediator connecting the simulation method to identification of the magnetic ground state.
Ab initio molecular dynamics provides an accurate description of electronic structure.
An accurate electronic-structure description obtained from ab initio molecular dynamics allows ferromagnetic ground states to be determined.
The predicted outcome is the presence or absence of a ferromagnetic ground state.
The method's accuracy and the applicability of the generalized gradient approximation limit the prediction.
Limitations of the simulation method and exchange-correlation functional introduce uncertainty into predictions of ferromagnetic ground states.
Magnetic moment and electronic structure are the proposed simulation observables.
A mismatch between simulated magnetic properties and the expected ferromagnetic ground state would falsify the hypothesis.
